MAJOR: `Audit` now silently drops events on a full channel (`default:` branch); a burst of /memory ops loses security audit records with only a counter/log, trading the prior unbounded-goroutine finding for audit-integrity loss against the AC-1 structured-audit contract.

`Audit` after `Close` sends on a closed channel and panics; there is no closed-state guard, and the diff does not show the HTTP server draining before `Close()`, so in-flight requests during shutdown can crash the process or lose their audit events.

The async worker holds no reference to stop accepting once shutdown begins: `Close()` waits for drain but any late `Audit` either panics (closed channel) or is dropped, so shutdown-time audit completeness is not guaranteed.
MINOR: No test covers the new worker/drop/Close paths: `memory_audit_dropped_total`, channel-full behavior, and drain-on-close are all untested, so the delta's core observability/reliability change can regress undetected.

`defer s.memoryAuditor.Close()` is registered early; any later-registered `st.Close()` (or equivalent) runs first under LIFO, so the final audit batch may flush against an already-closed PgStore and be lost — shutdown ordering should be explicit.
Dropped-event log omits `actor`/`record` fields present in the sibling audit logs, hindering correlation when auditing is degraded (the exact condition where it matters most).
[OUT_OF_SCOPE] `write` still silently skips when `e.TenantID == ""` with no metric — pre-existing behavior carried over, not introduced by this delta.
NIT: Channel capacity `256` is a hard-coded magic number with no rationale or configurability; document or derive it from expected burst sizing.
`closeOnce` guards double-`Close` but does nothing for the concurrent `Audit`-during-`Close` race, giving a false sense of shutdown safety.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly resolves the prior unbounded-goroutine, shutdown-drain, and half-finished role-posture findings (super/bypassrls now asserted), which is the right direction.
Top risks introduced: audit events dropped under load and a send-on-closed-channel panic during shutdown — both weaken the AC-1 audit evidence the item relies on.
Ship only after adding a non-panicking close path, a defined drop/fallback policy (or blocking with bounded timeout), and tests for the worker lifecycle.
